examples.en: My uncle got his high school diploma through an equivalency exam.

examples.ko: 검정고시는 일 년에 두 번 있어요.
examples.en: The equivalency exam is held twice a year.
She prepared for the equivalency exam while working.

examples.ko: 검정고시에 합격해서 대학에 갈 수 있게 됐어요.
examples.en: I passed the equivalency exam, so I could go to university.

examples.ko: 나이가 많아도 검정고시는 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can take the equivalency exam even if you are older.

examples.ko: 검정고시 학원에는 다양한 나이의 사람들이 다녀요.
examples.en: People of many ages attend the equivalency exam academy.

explain: 학교를 다니지 못했거나 중간에 그만둔 사람이 초등학교·중학교·고등학교 졸업 자격을 얻는 시험이에요. 보통 '검정고시를 보다', '검정고시에 합격하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: This is the exam people take when they missed or left school and still want an elementary, middle or high school graduation qualification. The usual verbs are 검정고시를 보다 and 검정고시에 합격하다.

examples.en: While driving at night, I saw a water deer on the road.
In the countryside, water deer come down into the fields.

examples.ko: 고라니 울음소리가 무서워서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The water deer's cry was so scary that I couldn't sleep.
A water deer jumped out in front of the car on the mountain road.
A water deer looks like a deer but has no antlers.
The farmers worry a lot because of water deer.

explain: 사슴과 비슷하게 생겼지만 다른 동물이에요. 시골길이나 논밭 이야기, 도로에서 차에 치이는 '로드킬' 뉴스에 나오기도 해요.
explain_en: It looks like a deer but is a different animal. It comes up in stories about country roads and fields, and in news about roadkill.

examples.ko: 그 식당은 십 년 동안 같은 맛을 고수했어요.
examples.en: That restaurant stuck to the same taste for ten years.
The boss holds on to his opinion to the end.
If you only stick to the old way, it's hard to improve.
To keep the price, they didn't offer discounts.

examples.ko: 그는 처음 약속한 입장을 고수하고 있어요.
examples.en: He is holding to the position he first promised.

examples.ko: 무조건 고수하지 말고 다른 방법도 생각해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't just insist no matter what; think of other ways too.

explain: '지키다'와 비슷하지만 의견, 입장, 방식을 바꾸지 않고 버틴다는 느낌이 강해요. 좋게 쓸 수도 있고 고집을 비판할 때도 써요. 바둑 '고수'와는 소리만 같은 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It is close to '지키다', but it carries a stronger sense of holding firm to an opinion, position or method without changing. It can be positive or critical of stubbornness. It is a different word from '고수' in Go, which only sounds the same.

examples.en: My mother likes precious metals like gold rings.
I ordered wedding rings at a jewelry shop.

examples.ko: 귀금속은 값이 비싸서 잘 보관해야 해요.
examples.en: Precious metals are expensive, so they must be stored well.
A thief stole jewelry from the house.
Gold and silver are typical precious metals.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때는 귀금속을 많이 가져가지 않아요.
examples.en: I do not bring much jewelry when I travel.

explain: 금, 은, 백금처럼 값이 많이 나가는 금속과 그것으로 만든 장신구를 같이 부를 때 써요. 값싼 '액세서리'와는 느낌이 달라요. 가게 간판에는 '귀금속'이나 '금은방'이 많이 붙어 있어요.
explain_en: It covers valuable metals like gold, silver, and platinum, plus jewelry made from them. It feels different from cheap '액세서리'. Shop signs often say '귀금속' or '금은방'.

examples.en: I met the final boss in the last stage of the game.
You need a lot of practice to reach the final stage.

examples.ko: 축구 경기 끝판에 골이 두 개나 나왔어요.
examples.en: Two goals came in the final stretch of the soccer game.
As the end drew near, everyone got nervous.
The last stage is always the hardest.
I felt great after clearing the last stage.

explain: 경기, 게임, 일에서 마지막 단계나 마지막 무렵을 가리켜요. '마지막'보다 입말에 가깝고 가벼워요. 비슷한 '막판'은 승부가 갈리는 마지막 순간에 더 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: The final boss of this game is really strong.
phrases.nuance_ko: 게임의 마지막 적을 말하고, 어떤 분야에서 가장 센 것을 비유하기도 해요. 예: 매운맛의 끝판왕.
phrases.nuance_en: The last enemy in a game; also figuratively the ultimate in some field, as in the final boss of spicy food.

explain_en: It refers to the last stage or last stretch of a match, game, or task. It is more spoken and casual than 마지막. The similar 막판 fits better for the final moment when a result is decided.

examples.en: It's cold, and on top of that, the wind is blowing too.

examples.ko: 몸도 안 좋은데 더더구나 일까지 많아요.
examples.en: I don't feel well, and on top of that I have a lot of work.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 비싸고 더더구나 색도 마음에 안 들어요.
examples.en: This outfit is expensive, and moreover I don't even like the color.

examples.ko: 저는 요리를 못하는데 더더구나 오늘은 재료도 없어요.
examples.en: I'm bad at cooking, and what's more, I have no ingredients today.

examples.ko: 길도 막히고 더더구나 비까지 와서 늦었어요.
examples.en: The roads were jammed, and on top of that it rained, so I was late.

examples.ko: 더더구나 이렇게 늦은 시간에는 갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: Especially at such a late hour, I can't go.

explain: '더구나'를 더 힘주어 말하는 느낌이에요. 앞의 이야기에 더해서 상황이 더 심해지거나 더 그렇다는 걸 덧붙일 때 써요. 말할 때는 '게다가'나 '더구나'로 바꿔도 돼요.
explain_en: It feels like a more emphatic version of '더구나'. Use it to add that, on top of what you just said, the situation is even more so. In speech you can swap it for '게다가' or '더구나'.

examples.en: A vine is growing along the fence.
I rested for a while under the grapevine.
The vine wraps around the tree and climbs up.
Small pumpkins grew on the pumpkin vine.
A rose vine covered the wall.

examples.ko: 덩굴을 자르지 않으면 집을 다 덮어요.
examples.en: If you don't cut the vine, it will cover the whole house.

explain: 포도, 호박, 장미처럼 줄기가 길게 뻗거나 다른 것을 감고 자라는 식물에 써요. '덩굴'과 '넝쿨'은 둘 다 표준어예요. '덩쿨'은 틀린 표기라서 조심하세요.
explain_en: It is used for plants like grapes, pumpkins and roses whose stems stretch long or wind around other things. Both '덩굴' and '넝쿨' are standard words. '덩쿨' is a wrong spelling, so watch out.

examples.en: I heard a woodpecker in the forest.
A woodpecker is pecking at a tree.
Woodpeckers make holes in trees with their beaks.

examples.ko: 산에서 딱따구리를 직접 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever seen a woodpecker in person in the mountains?
A woodpecker's beak is very hard.

examples.ko: 딱따구리가 만든 구멍에 다른 새가 살기도 해요.
examples.en: Sometimes other birds live in holes made by woodpeckers.

explain: 나무를 쪼아 구멍을 내는 새예요. 철자를 '딱다구리'로 잘못 쓰기 쉬운데 표준어는 '딱따구리'예요.
explain_en: It is a bird that pecks holes in trees. People often misspell it as '딱다구리', but the standard form is '딱따구리'.

examples.en: We take a mock exam at school tomorrow.
My mock test score went up from last month.
I checked my skills with a Korean mock test.

examples.ko: 모의고사는 진짜 시험처럼 시간을 재서 풀어요.
examples.en: You solve a mock test with a timer, like the real exam.

examples.ko: 모의고사가 끝나고 친구들과 답을 맞춰 봤어요.
examples.en: After the mock test, I compared answers with friends.

examples.ko: 고3 학생들은 수능 전에 모의고사를 여러 번 봐요.
examples.en: Third-year high school students take mock tests several times before the CSAT.

explain: 진짜 시험을 미리 연습하는 시험이에요. 한국 고등학생은 대학 시험을 준비하며 '모의고사'를 자주 봐요. 그냥 시험 연습은 '연습 문제'나 '시험 연습'이라고 하고, '모의고사'는 시험 형식을 그대로 따라 한 시험이에요.
explain_en: A practice exam that copies the real one. Korean high school students take many '모의고사' while preparing for the college entrance exam. Ordinary practice questions are '연습 문제'; a '모의고사' follows the real test format.

examples.en: Teenagers sometimes rebel against their parents.
That child defied the teacher.
The mother is worried because of her defiant son.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때 이유 없이 반항했어요.
examples.en: As a kid, I rebelled for no reason.
I thought it was useless to rebel.
It's a movie where the main character rebels against society.

explain: '부모님께 반항하다', '선생님께 반항하다'처럼 윗사람의 말을 따르지 않고 맞서는 일에 써요. '반대하다'는 의견이 다르다는 뜻이고, '반항하다'는 태도나 행동으로 대드는 느낌이 더 강해요. 같은 뜻의 명사 '반항'은 '반항기'처럼 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is used for pushing back against authority, as in 부모님께 반항하다. 반대하다 only means disagreeing, whereas 반항하다 is more about attitude and behavior that talks back. The noun 반항 also appears in words like 반항기 (rebellious phase).

examples.en: Around dawn today the rain suddenly stopped.
When dawn came, the weather turned chilly.
We reached the mountain top around daybreak.

examples.ko: 새벽녘까지 시험 공부를 하느라 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I studied for the exam until dawn and couldn't sleep.
The streets at daybreak are quiet and clear.
I woke up around dawn and opened the window.

explain: '새벽'은 시간대 전체를 말하고, '새벽녘'은 날이 밝아 올 무렵을 가리켜요. '새벽녘에'처럼 때를 나타낼 때 많이 써요. 비슷한 모양의 '해 질 녘'은 해가 질 무렵이에요.
explain_en: '새벽' covers the whole early-morning period, while '새벽녘' points to the time when day is about to break. It is used in the form '새벽녘에' to say when something happened. The similar '해 질 녘' means around sunset.

examples.ko: 어린이집 알림장에는 오늘 아이가 친구와 블록 놀이를 했다고 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: The daycare notebook says my child played with blocks with a friend today.
The teacher wrote the things to bring in the notice notebook.
Be sure to show the notice notebook to your parents.
Please check today's notice notebook and sign it.
I forgot to write the homework in my notice notebook.
I looked at my child's notebook, and it says there is a field trip tomorrow.

explain: 어린이집, 유치원, 초등학교에서 선생님이 부모님께 전하는 소식이나 숙제, 준비물을 적는 공책이에요. '알림장을 쓰다', '알림장을 확인하다'처럼 써요. 요즘은 앱으로 보내는 경우도 있어서 '알림장 앱'이라는 말도 써요.
explain_en: It is the notebook used at daycare, kindergarten and elementary school for teachers to write news, homework and things to bring for parents. It goes with '알림장을 쓰다' and '알림장을 확인하다'. Nowadays some schools send it through an app, so you also hear '알림장 앱'.

examples.en: Please press firmly on the wound with a cloth.

examples.ko: 상대 팀이 높이 올라와 우리를 압박했어요.
examples.en: The other team came forward and pressured us.

examples.ko: 상사가 계속 결과를 내라고 압박해서 스트레스를 받아요.
examples.en: My boss keeps pressing for results, which stresses me.

examples.ko: 너무 압박하지 말고 시간을 좀 주세요.
examples.en: Don't pressure me so much, please give me some time.
There's a client who pushes us to lower the price.

examples.ko: 코치가 선수들을 압박하면 오히려 실수가 늘어요.
examples.en: If the coach pressures the players, mistakes actually increase.

explain: '누르다'는 손이나 물건으로 힘을 줄 때 써요. '압박하다'는 상처를 누르는 것처럼 실제로 누를 때와, 마음이나 상황으로 몰아붙일 때 둘 다 써요. '재촉하다'보다 부담이 크게 느껴질 때가 많아요.
explain_en: '누르다' is applying force with a hand or object. '압박하다' covers both really pressing, like on a wound, and pushing someone through mood or circumstances. It often feels heavier than '재촉하다' (to hurry someone).

examples.ko: 그 아이는 어려도 약아서 손해 보는 일이 없어요.
examples.en: That kid is young but shrewd and never loses out.
If you act calculating, your friends won't like it.

examples.ko: 동생은 약아요. 심부름은 늘 저한테 시켜요.
examples.en: My younger brother is sly. He always makes me run the errands.
A shrewd person looks after their own interests first.

examples.ko: 그 가게 주인은 약아서 속기 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: The shop owner is sharp, so it's hard to trick him.

examples.ko: 너무 약아 보이는 사람은 믿기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to trust someone who looks too calculating.

explain: '똑똑하다'는 머리가 좋다는 칭찬이고, '약다'는 자기 이익을 잘 챙기는 영리함이라 칭찬이 아닐 때가 많아요. '영악하다', '꾀바르다'와 비슷하지만 '약다'가 더 가볍고 일상적이에요.
explain_en: '똑똑하다' praises intelligence, while '약다' means being clever at protecting your own interest, so it is often not a compliment. It is close to '영악하다' and '꾀바르다' but lighter and more everyday.

p.n: 약다 means shrewd and self-serving; 명석하다 is plain praise for a sharp mind.

examples.en: The shepherd came down from the mountain driving his sheep.
Do you know the story of the boy who cried wolf?
When I was little, my dream was to be a shepherd.
A shepherd and a dog guard the sheep together.

examples.ko: 저 양치기는 하루 종일 풀밭에서 일해요.
examples.en: That shepherd works in the meadow all day.
The shepherd in the movie played a pipe.

explain: '양치기'는 양을 돌보는 사람이에요. 소를 돌보는 사람은 '소치기'라고 하지만 쓰임은 드물어요. '양치기 소년'은 거짓말하는 사람을 말할 때 비유로도 자주 써요. '양치질'과는 완전히 달라요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 약속을 안 지켜서 양치기 소년이 됐어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거짓말을 자주 해서 진짜 말해도 믿어 주지 않는 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: It points to someone who lies so often that nobody believes them even when they tell the truth.

explain_en: '양치기' is a person who tends sheep. '양치기 소년' is also used as a metaphor for someone who lies. It is unrelated to '양치질', which means brushing your teeth.

examples.en: I bought the fabric after roughly guessing the length.

examples.ko: 정확한 숫자를 몰라서 어림짐작할 수밖에 없어요.
examples.en: I don't know the exact number, so all I can do is guess.

examples.ko: 사람이 몇 명 왔는지 어림짐작해 보세요.
examples.en: Try to guess how many people came.
I guessed just from the look on their face, but I was wrong.

examples.ko: 어림짐작하지 말고 직접 재 보는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: Don't just guess; it's better to measure it yourself.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 가격을 어림짐작하는 데 익숙해요.
examples.en: He is used to estimating prices by eye.

explain: 정확히 재거나 계산하지 않고 대강 짐작할 때 써요. 근거가 부족하다는 느낌이 있어서 '어림짐작으로 말하다'처럼 약간 조심스럽거나 부정적으로 들릴 수 있어요. '대충 어림잡다'도 비슷하게 써요.
explain_en: It is used when you guess roughly without measuring or calculating exactly. It implies weak grounds, so '어림짐작으로 말하다' can sound a bit cautious or negative. '어림잡다' is used in a similar way.

examples.en: The teacher generously laughed off the child's mistake.
I just laughed off my friend's teasing.

examples.ko: 그 정도 실수는 웃어넘길 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can laugh off a mistake like that.
You shouldn't laugh off serious matters.

examples.ko: 그는 내 질문을 웃어넘기고 대답하지 않았어요.
examples.en: He laughed off my question and didn't answer.

examples.ko: 사소한 일은 그냥 웃어넘기는 편이 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better to just laugh off small things.

explain: 문제를 심각하게 받아들이지 않고 웃으면서 지나갈 때 써요. 너그럽게 넘어간다는 좋은 뜻도 있고, 해야 할 말을 피한다는 느낌도 있어서 상황에 따라 달라져요.
explain_en: Use it when someone passes over a problem with a laugh instead of taking it seriously. It can mean being generous and easygoing, or it can feel like dodging something that should be addressed, depending on the situation.

examples.en: On rainy days, I shop in the underground mall.
The underground mall is cool in summer and warm in winter.
I bought cheap, pretty clothes at the underground mall.
I don't know where the entrance to the underground mall is.
I walked once around the underground mall with my friend.

examples.ko: 이 지하상가는 길이 복잡해서 자주 길을 잃어요.
examples.en: The paths in this underground mall are complicated, so I often get lost.

explain: 지하철역 근처 지하 통로를 따라 가게가 쭉 이어진 곳을 말해요. 백화점이나 마트의 '지하 매장'과는 달리 여러 작은 가게가 모여 있는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It refers to a place where many shops line an underground passage, often near a subway station. Unlike the basement floor of a department store or mart, it feels like a cluster of many small shops.

examples.en: Don't cling too much to things in the past.
He is far too fixated on test scores.

examples.ko: 친구는 새 휴대폰에 집착해서 하루 종일 만져요.
examples.en: My friend is obsessed with the new phone and touches it all day.
If you fixate on small mistakes, your mind gets tired.

examples.ko: 한 가지에 집착하는 습관을 고치고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to fix my habit of fixating on one thing.
I used to be obsessed with replies.

explain: '좋아하다'는 좋은 마음이고, '집착하다'는 한 가지에 너무 매달려서 힘들 정도라는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 사랑, 돈, 결과 등에 '~에 집착하다'로 말해요. 긍정적으로 푹 빠지는 것은 '몰두하다'예요.
explain_en: 좋아하다 is a positive feeling; 집착하다 has a negative feel of clinging to one thing so hard it becomes painful. Say '~에 집착하다' for love, money, or results. Being positively absorbed is 몰두하다.

examples.en: There are a lot of oak trees in the mountains.
Acorns fall from the oak tree.
Meat grilled over oak charcoal tastes good.
We rested under an old oak tree.

examples.ko: 이 집은 참나무로 만든 가구가 많아요.
examples.en: This house has a lot of furniture made of oak.

examples.ko: 가을이 되면 참나무 잎이 갈색으로 변해요.
examples.en: In autumn, oak leaves turn brown.

explain: 참나무는 한 종류가 아니라 상수리나무·떡갈나무·갈참나무처럼 도토리가 열리는 여러 나무를 묶어 부르는 말이에요. '참나무 숯'은 고기 구울 때 좋은 숯으로 알려져 있어요. 영어의 oak와 완전히 같지는 않지만 비슷하게 번역해요.
explain_en: 참나무 is not one species but a group name for acorn-bearing trees such as 상수리나무, 떡갈나무, and 갈참나무. '참나무 숯' is known as good charcoal for grilling meat. It is translated as oak, though it is not exactly the same.

examples.en: I'm looking for a job before I graduate.

examples.ko: 좋은 취직자리가 나서 친구가 아주 기뻐해요.
examples.en: A good job opening came up, and my friend is very happy.

examples.ko: 삼촌이 제 취직자리를 하나 소개해 줬어요.
examples.en: My uncle introduced me to a job opening.
It isn't easy to find a job these days.
There aren't many job openings in this city.
I asked my senior about job openings.

explain: '일자리'와 비슷하지만 '취직자리'는 직장에 들어가서 일하게 될 자리라는 느낌이 있어요. 보통 '취직자리를 구하다/알아보다/소개하다'로 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '일자리', but '취직자리' carries the feel of a position you get by entering a company. It usually appears as '취직자리를 구하다/알아보다/소개하다' (look for/check/recommend).

examples.ko: 치사스럽게 그것 하나 가지고 화를 내요?
examples.en: Are you getting angry over just that one thing, how petty?

examples.ko: 친구가 천 원 때문에 계속 따져서 치사스러웠어요.
examples.en: My friend kept arguing over one thousand won, and it felt petty.
I don't want to win by a petty method.
What will you do being so petty like that?
My younger brother acts petty over a single snack.

examples.ko: 치사스러운 말은 하지 말고 솔직하게 얘기해요.
examples.en: Don't say petty things, let's talk honestly.

explain: '치사스럽다'는 작은 일에 쩨쩨하게 굴거나 비겁하게 행동하는 것에 쓰는 말이에요. 같은 뜻으로 '치사하다'를 더 자주 말해요. 친구끼리 가볍게 투덜댈 때 쓰지만 윗사람에게는 하지 않아요.
explain_en: 치사스럽다 describes acting stingy over small things or behaving in a low, cowardly way. 치사하다 is used more often for the same meaning. Friends use it casually when grumbling, but you don't say it to someone older.

examples.ko: 저는 이번 달에 동호회에서 탈퇴하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to leave the club this month.
If you cancel your app membership, your records disappear.
My friend suddenly left the group chat.

examples.ko: 이 서비스에서 탈퇴하는 방법을 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me how to leave this service.

examples.ko: 이 사이트를 탈퇴해도 다시 가입할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even if you leave this site, you can sign up again.

examples.ko: 마음이 바뀌어서 탈퇴하려고 했는데 못 했어요.
examples.en: I changed my mind and tried to withdraw, but I couldn't.

explain: 모임, 사이트, 단체의 회원 자격을 스스로 그만둘 때 써요. 가입하는 것은 '가입하다'이고, 학교나 직장을 그만두는 것은 '그만두다'를 써서 구별해요. 내보낼 때는 '제명하다'를 써요.
explain_en: Use it when you give up membership of a group, site, or organization. Joining is '가입하다', and quitting a school or job is '그만두다', so they are kept separate. Expelling someone is '제명하다'.

examples.en: I'll finish my homework quickly and go out to play.
I'm hungry, so I'll eat dinner quickly and head out.
The time flew by.
I got the cleaning done in a flash and rested.
I'll be right back, so please wait.
I washed up quickly in the morning and left home.

explain: '빨리'보다 입말에 가깝고, 일을 가볍게 서둘러 끝내는 느낌이에요. 비슷한 '얼른'은 지금 바로 하라고 재촉할 때도 많이 써요. 격식 있는 글이나 윗사람에게는 '빨리'가 더 안전해요.
explain_en: It is closer to spoken language than 빨리 and feels like getting something done lightly and fast. The similar 얼른 is also often used to urge someone to do something right now. In formal writing or with elders, 빨리 is safer.

dis.h: in a flash; colloquial, finish a task

p.n: 후딱 is colloquial and means done in a flash, with a light feel.

examples.en: Every evening I spin a hula hoop for thirty minutes.
The hula hoop keeps falling off my waist.

examples.ko: 아이들이 마당에서 훌라후프 놀이를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: The kids are playing with hula hoops in the yard.
If you exercise with a hula hoop, you sweat a lot.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 훌라후프를 열 번도 못 돌렸어요.
examples.en: As a kid, I couldn't spin a hula hoop even ten times.

examples.ko: 친구가 생일 선물로 훌라후프를 사 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend bought me a hula hoop as a birthday present.

explain: 허리로 돌리는 큰 고리예요. '훌라후프를 돌리다'처럼 '돌리다'와 함께 써요. 철자는 '훌라후프'로 쓰고 '훌라우프'가 아니에요.
explain_en: It is the big ring you spin around your waist, and it goes with '돌리다', as in '훌라후프를 돌리다'. The spelling is '훌라후프', not '훌라우프'.
